candidates.title: TBCCL: Running Qwen 27B across Apple Silicon and NVIDIA GPUs over Thunderbolt 4
candidates.summary:
Hello!
I’ve been working on a project called TBCCL, which started out as an experiment to see if I could use my Mac mini M4 and an NVIDIA laptop together for distributed training and inference.

My setup consists of a Mac mini M4 (16GB unified memory) and an RTX 3070 Ti laptop (8GB VRAM) running Linux, connected directly over Thunderbolt 4.

I wanted a way to communicate between different operating systems and accelerators without having to build a separate transport for every framework.

candidates.title: Two models on one 8 GB GPU: making the LLM wait for the TTS after every sentence stopped my voice assistant from stuttering
candidates.summary:
I wanted ESP32 voice-assistant boards running the open-source xiaozhi firmware to hold real conversations fully offline, served from a laptop with an RTX 4060 Laptop GPU (8 GB) and 16 GB of RAM. I tested it with an M5Stack Atom EchoS3R and a Stack-chan; it isn’t tied to one board. The pipeline is the usual one: VAD and ASR on the CPU, then an LLM (Gemma 4 E4B, QAT q4_0, on llama.cpp) writes the answer while a voice-cloning TTS (Qwen3-TTS 1.7B, F16 GGUF) speaks it sentence by sentence.

Fitting both models into 8 GB was the first problem. Getting them to share it was the real one.
